A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RPG/ZeroRepo study and include readable Appendices A–E. Text, equations, tables, and figures can be matched across rewriting, renumbering, and layout changes, without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original RepoCraft evaluations of ZeroRepo and baselines, localization ablations, scaling experiments, and appendix analyses of generated repositories.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark performance in Table 2, the localization ablation in Table 4, and detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: Both retain the same feature-tree exploration and retrieval, RPG construction, topological code generation, localization, and testing procedures. Algorithms 1–4 and the appendix prompts and tools are unchanged; shortened descriptions do not establish a procedural revision.

E1.justification: Both use the same six Python repository tasks and 1,052 evaluation tasks in RepoCraft, with the same EpiCoder feature ontology. The repository domains, task requirements, and supplementary test scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 and Appendix E.2 retain MetaGPT, ChatDev, Paper2Code, OpenHands, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Claude Code CLI, and Gold Projects. Table 4 retains the same comparison against ZeroRepo without graph guidance.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes the 30-iteration statement from terminal-agent runs in v1 to 'all runs' in v5. However, unchanged Appendix E.1 still specifies default multi-agent/workflow configurations and 30 iterations for terminal agents. This leaves unclear whether the budget scope was revised or the wording merely generalized; other stated metrics, backbones, and evaluation procedures match.

E4.justification: The scaling studies, graph-guidance ablation, feature-distribution and code-structure analyses, generated-test coverage study, and coverage/novelty/localization examples are retained. Appendix movements and figure renumbering do not introduce or remove analyses.

E5.justification: Both report mean ± SD in Tables 4 and 8 and retain identical uncertainty displays in the plots. Table 4 only reduces decimal precision; v5 adds no seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Section 6 change the reported code-scale multiplier over 'other baselines' from 64× to 68×, without changing Table 2's underlying values. Benchmark and appendix result entries otherwise match, and Table 4's numerical edits are equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: The coverage and novelty definitions and equations (1)–(2), sampling mathematics, and algorithmic pseudocode are retained. No new or revised theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The headline code-scale advantage over other baselines is modestly strengthened from 64× to 68×. The RPG, ZeroRepo, and RepoCraft contributions and the main coverage, correctness, scaling, and localization claims retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: The introduction tempers its causal framing: v1 says natural-language planning limitations yield two failure modes, whereas v5 says they 'can more easily lead to' them and functionalities are 'sometimes' incomplete. Existing mechanism explanations and the test-generation bottleneck discussed in Appendix C.5 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Prompt templates, tool signatures, skeleton/code examples, Docker testing details, and Section 5.3's debugging, localization, voting, and remediation limits are retained. Model identities were already documented in v1, and no code/data access or resource disclosure is added.

R1.justification: v5 substitutes the GPT-4o System Card and Gemini 2.5 technical report for product-page references and explicitly includes Gemini CLI in the industrial-agent discussion. The broader positioning against natural-language planning and relationships to earlier graph, multi-agent, and workflow approaches remain stable.

P1.justification: The abstract and several introduction, setup, and analysis paragraphs are rewritten or condensed, and author order and contact/internship notes are updated. The section sequence, detailed method exposition, conclusion, and most appendix text remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is lightly redrawn and relabeled, Table 4 is enlarged and its rows reordered, and several captions and float placements change. Table 5 moves and Figures 7–8 exchange numbers; the empirical plots themselves remain identical.

improvement.justification: v5 explains the two planning levels more directly in the abstract, qualifies the introduction's failure claims, and makes Table 4 easier to read. These provide limited clarity and presentation gains while the method and empirical support remain stable. Ambiguous budget wording and the unexplained 64× to 68× revision limit the improvement.
